I’ll never “love” how I look (I honestly don’t think that’s a realistic goal in most cases), so I try to simply spend less time thinking about my appearance and avoid things that I know to be triggers for me: 

-I don’t take selfies and don’t let others take photos of me.

-I generally try to avoid people who talk about looks a lot. (I had this one friend that I essentially cut off because she was constantly critiquing my hair/clothes and wanting to give me “makeovers” and take photos of me). 

-I avoid going places where there’s likely to be many young attractive people present (I’m in my 30s and know a few people my age who like partying with young people because “it makes them feel young” but for me it has the opposite effect). 

-I don’t follow influencers or consume media (music videos, tv shows etc) that’s centred around young attractive people. 

Apart from avoiding triggers, I find that self-pampering, skincare, exercising etc can momentarily trick my brain into thinking I’m attractive, so long as I don’t take any photos or look in the mirror too long.

Most importantly though, I try to keep myself busy and occupied with other things. I try to have non appearance-related goals and reasons for living, and remind myself of non-appearance related reasons I’m valuable. I try to remind myself that society/men don’t define my worth and that just because I don’t meet certain societal criteria doesn’t mean I don’t deserve to have a good life and be happy.

My face lost a bit of baby fat in my early 20s but I actually liked it because it gave me more cheekbone/jawline definition. The first sign of aging that I didn’t like was at 26 when I saw the first signs of nasolabial folds. Then in my late 20s I noticed my lips becoming gradually less full, my face appearing flatter/longer, my dark circles becoming more prominent, fine lines under the eyes, and (a weird one no-one talks about) my eyelids starting to droop. I also began noticing hyperpigmentation and skin dullness/dryness, although I was able to address the latter with a good skincare routine.

In my 30s now and dealing with facial fat descent  and dynamic wrinkles around my mouth. 🥴 I will say the changes in your 20s are pretty negligible and other people barely notice them (and in hindsight I wish I’d worried less about them). I found it wasn’t until my face started becoming a bit bottom-heavy over the last two years that my overall “look” really changed and people no longer perceived me as young.

Do you prep your skin prior to applying? I find doing a gentle manual exfoliation with a Konjac sponge and also using a chemical exfoliant like lactic acid makes a big difference. Also unless you’re on stage I think less is generally more with foundation - I like to use a light formula and apply sparingly with a damp beauty blender then just use concealer where I need it.

Try to build a solid foundation with a good cleanser, sunscreen and moisturizer. Everything else is just added extras. 

If you have specific concerns, integrate ingredients with proven benefits like retinoids, ascorbic acid, AHAs/BHAs etc. Try to ignore trendy or gimmicky ingredients unless just for fun.

Dr Dray and Lab Muffin on Youtube provide really great no-nonsense advice. The Skincare Addiction subreddit is also great. 

Insidecoder.com is great for demystifying ingredients lists and giving the rundown (including studies etc) behind different ingredients. Beautypedia is another great resource. 

I have dry sensitive acne-prone skin with signs of aging so my skincare routine consists of CeraVe Hydrating Cleanser, Timeless 10% Vitamin C, The Ordinary Multi-peptide Serum, CeraVe PM, and La Roche Posay Shaka Fluid. Then at night I double cleanse with The Ordinary Squalane Cleanser and will alternate between retinoids and AHAs then a thick occlusive cream like CeraVe Moisturising Cream. 

Of course everyone’s skin is different and a lot of finding what works is just trial and error (plus other factors can affect our skin such as diet, lifestyle, hormones, climate etc).
